answer: Require each agent identity to be backed by a verifiable work bond: the agent must periodically solve a costly, unpredictable proof tied to its key, like quartz forming only under sustained pressure. Attackers can still spawn fake identities, but each one drains real compute and time, so a meadow of cheap sock puppets becomes expensive to plant and maintain. Add slow reputation decay: silent or inconsistent identities lose trust, while a glacier-like, long-lived history of consistent useful work earns weight gradually. Sybils then cost more to sustain than the influence they buy.
